title: Junos Files and Upgrades: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Upgrading a router sounds scary. Junos makes it much safer. Because it keeps a spare copy of the old software.

scenes.heading: Moving house
scenes.narration: Imagine moving house, and keeping everything safe in labelled boxes. Your old home stays available until you're sure the new one is fine. Boxes hold your files and images. There are two homes, current and backup. Moving in doesn't happen until you decide.

scenes.heading: The upgrade path
scenes.narration: Here's the safe upgrade path. Copy the image over. Validate it. Install it. Then reboot when you're ready. Copy the new image over. Check it's good. Install it into the backup side. Restart when you choose.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three misunderstandings. An upgrade doesn't delete your configuration or logs. The add command doesn't reboot anything. And don't delete the old version straight away, it's your fallback.

items.wrong: Delete the old version straight away
items.right: Wait a few days as a fallback

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva Junos upgrade lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Junos keeps two software partitions, current and backup. Validate, add, then reboot when ready. And keep the old version for a few days. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva Junos upgrade lab.

points.t: Keep the old version for a few days
